findings.detail: pinned reading: For the inverse-defined field $\bq$, the direct remainder hypotheses mean the displayed moment hypotheses, with the smooth-field inequalities applied to $\bq_\eta$ before taking $\eta\downarrow0$. (The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:balanced-Stein-sufficient-conditions} constructs smooth ridge fields with integrable dominators; the paragraph immediately following Lemma~\ref{lem:Stein-remainders-from-moments} explicitly prescribes this ridge approximation and Fatou passage.)

pinned reading: The identity $\pdv{\bq}{z_{ij}}=\bK\be_jr_i-\bL^\top\be_iq_j$ holds almost surely under the joint law of the random fields, for every $i=1,\ldots,n$ and $j=1,\ldots,d$. (The lemma assumes random matrices and vectors, and its proof takes expectations of the pointwise derivative-energy inequality.)

pinned reading: In the balanced-sketch calculations, $(\bS,\bA)$ denote the normalized quantities $(\overline{\bS},\overline{\bA})$ defined in Section~\ref{app:proof-setup}, so $\trace(\bA)=n$ almost surely. (Immediately before Assumption~\ref{assu:Gaussian-Stein-design}, Section~\ref{app:proof-setup} defines the normalized representative and explicitly reuses the sketch symbols for it from Section~\ref{app:balanced-transfer-setup} through Section~\ref{app:proof-trace-calibration-general}.)

pinned reading: There exists a deterministic $K_\varepsilon<\infty$, independent of $n$, such that $\sup_n\norm{\varepsilon_1}_{\psi_2}\leq K_\varepsilon$, where $\norm{W}_{\psi_2}:=\inf\{t>0:\E\exp(W^2/t^2)\leq2\}$. (Assumption~\ref{assu:Gaussian-Stein-design} explicitly states this uniform norm bound and defines the norm.)

pinned reading: There exists a deterministic $n_0\geq1$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, almost surely every positive eigenvalue of $n\bA/\trace(\bA)$ belongs to $[c_-,c_+]$ and $m-d\geq\kappa n$, with $c_-,c_+,\kappa$ deterministic and independent of $n$. (Assumption~\ref{assu:Gaussian-Stein-design} explicitly introduces deterministic constants including $n_0$ and states the spectral and dimension-gap conditions for every $n\geq n_0$.)

pinned reading: For the derivative versions defining $\calE_{\bq}$, the identity $\pdv{\bq}{z_{ij}}=\bK\be_jr_i-\bL^\top\be_iq_j$ holds almost surely under the law used by $\E$, simultaneously for $1\leq i\leq n$ and $1\leq j\leq d$. (Lemma~\ref{lem:derivative-energy-from-inverse-moments} passes from this identity to a pointwise bound on $\calE_{\bq}$ and then to its expected square; merely Lebesgue-null exceptions would not justify that passage for an unrestricted law.)

pinned reading: The expectation in $\E[\norm{\bep}^2(\norm{\bq}^2+\calE_{\bq})]\leq C_1n$ is unconditional over the joint law of $(\bZ,\bS,\bep)$. (Lemma~\ref{lem:Stein-remainders-from-moments} explicitly conditions its smoothness declaration, but writes both this moment hypothesis and its resulting bound on $\E\Xi_1^2$ using unconditioned expectations.)

pinned reading: On the almost-sure event $\rank(\bS)=m$, $(\bS\bS^\top)^{-1/2}$ denotes the unique symmetric positive definite square root of $(\bS\bS^\top)^{-1}$. (Standard positive definite matrix power notation in the observation-geometry display, followed immediately by the assertion that the row-whitened sketch satisfies $\bF\bF^\top=\bI_m$.)

(The recorded entry names the estimator without giving its defining minimization or inverse formula. Full column rank fixes uniqueness and the domain of the inverse representation.)

Later MSE expectations average estimation error over training data and sketch randomness without replacing $R$ by an unconditional risk.)
